subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 64-year-old man with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer is treated with a regimen that includes etoposide and cisplatin. After the first cycle he develops severe neutropenia. Analysis of his tumor cells shows accumulation of double-stranded DNA breaks and arrest in G2 phase.
question: Which of the following is the primary molecular target of etoposide?
explanation_correct: Etoposide and teniposide inhibit eukaryotic topoisomerase II, preventing resealing of the double-stranded break created to relieve supercoils and thereby generating DNA double-strand breaks that arrest the cell cycle and trigger apoptosis.

explanation_incorrect.B: Topoisomerase I is inhibited by irinotecan and topotecan, which produce single-stranded breaks.
explanation_incorrect.C: DNA gyrase is the bacterial topoisomerase II inhibited by fluoroquinolones.
explanation_incorrect.D: Ribonucleotide reductase is inhibited by hydroxyurea.

educationalObjective: Etoposide inhibits topoisomerase II and produces double-stranded DNA breaks.
